chuukese_semenkoror.name: holds and dispenses the deep, esoteric knowledge of the gods
chuukese_semenkoror.notes: Named among the Chuukese (Truk) gods as 'Father of Wisdom', a specialist deity of knowledge alongside Sinenap ('Skilled One') and Aremei ('Achiever').

circassian_shible.name: hurls the thunderbolt and strikes earth, beast and man with lightning
circassian_shible.notes: Adyghe thunder/lightning god; persons and animals he strikes are deemed blessed and specially chosen.

circassian_shible.name: sanctifies the place, tree or creature he strikes, making it a site of veneration
circassian_shible.notes: A grove or tree struck by Shible's bolt became holy ground for sacrifice and prayer.

circassian_setenaya.name: works sorcery and prophecy as the wise-woman and witch of the Narts
circassian_setenaya.notes: Setenay-guasche, matriarch of the Narts, combines eternal youth, beauty, wisdom and witchcraft; she advises, schemes and foresees for the whole host.

sources.reference: J. Colarusso, 'The Woman of the Myths: the Satanaya Cycle' (CircassianWorld)

circassian_setenaya.name: brings about and midwifes the miraculous births of the Nart heroes
circassian_setenaya.notes: Conceives or raises every major hero; cuts the glowing infant Sosruquo out of the stone after he is begotten upon it.

sources.reference: J. Colarusso, Nart Sagas from the Caucasus (Princeton, 2002)

circassian_sosruquo.name: is tempered in the smith's forge to a body of iron, invulnerable but at the knees/hips
circassian_sosruquo.notes: After Tlepsh quenches the glowing stone-born infant, his body becomes iron; the spot the tongs gripped remains his one vulnerable point.

sources.reference: Mythlok, 'Sosruko: The Fire-Forged Hero of the Nart Sagas'

circassian_mezitha.name: disposes of the fate of the wild beasts and grants luck to the hunt
circassian_mezitha.notes: Adyghe forest- and hunt-god (məz 'forest' + tḥə 'god'); he releases game to favored hunters and withholds it from the impious.

circassian_warzameg.name: leads the host as the Great Nart, eldest and foremost of the heroes
circassian_warzameg.notes: Warzameg/Wozermes is styled the 'Great Nart', husband of Setenaya, around whose hearth the saga cycles turn.

sources.reference: J. Colarusso, Nart Sagas from the Caucasus (Princeton, 2002)

circassian_tha.name: begets and orders the entire universe as the single supreme god
circassian_tha.notes: Theshxwe ('Great God') is the monistic high god from whom the cosmos issues; the lesser tha are his manifestations.

circassian_psathha.name: grants the breath-soul (psa) and keeps the souls of the dead in the world beyond
circassian_psathha.notes: Name = psa ('soul/life') + tha ('god'); the souls of the dead pass to the otherworld (hedrixe) under his charge and watch over their descendants.

cree_wisahkecahk.name: shifts his own shape and the shapes and natures of the animals at will
cree_wisahkecahk.notes: The Algonquian transformer changes form and fixes the appearance and behaviour of the creatures in the âtayôhkêwin sacred stories.

crow_old_man_coyote.name: travels east to west shaping land, mountains, rivers, animals and plants and giving them life
crow_old_man_coyote.notes: After the earth is raised, Old Man Coyote forms and animates the whole created world on his journey across it.

sources.reference: Lib @ Little Big Horn College, 'Creation Story'

dacian_decaeneus.name: teaches astronomy, the courses of the heavens and divine prognostics to the Getae
dacian_decaeneus.notes: Strabo: Decaeneus, who had studied among the Egyptians, taught the Getae physics, ethics, logic and the revolutions of the heavens, foretelling the divine will.

dacian_decaeneus.name: imposes law, sober discipline and obedience, persuading the Getae to uproot their vines
dacian_decaeneus.notes: As high priest and coadjutor of Burebista he legislated the wine-abstention and Pythagorean-style discipline of the realm.

dacian_burebista.name: unifies the Getic and Dacian tribes and raises a great empire by training and discipline
dacian_burebista.notes: Strabo: Burebista restored a people ruined by wars and within a few years built a great power through sobriety and obedience to his commands.

dayak_jata.name: rules the underworld and primeval waters as the great water-serpent (Tambon)
dayak_jata.notes: Jata Balawang Bulau, female lower-world power appearing as dragon/water-snake; one in essence with Mahatala, of whom she is the shadow.

dayak_tempon_telon.name: ferries the souls of the dead in the soul-ship past dangers to the highest heaven
dayak_tempon_telon.notes: Divine ferryman who conveys the liau of the deceased, freed by the Tiwah ceremony, to Lewu Tatau, the heaven of Ranying.

dine_johonaai.name: carries the turquoise sun across the sky each day from his house in the east
dine_johonaai.notes: The Sun-bearer of the Diné Bahaneʼ, husband of Changing Woman, who bears the sun-disk on its daily course.

dine_johonaai.name: tests the Hero Twins with four ordeals and arms them with lightning to slay the monsters
dine_johonaai.notes: After the twins prove their paternity he gives them lightning arrows and weapons to destroy the Naayééʼ.

dinka_deng.name: sends the rain and strikes with lightning as the foremost free-divinity of the sky
dinka_deng.notes: Deng (Dengdit) is the sky-power of rain and fertility, son of Abuk in some genealogies, invoked for rain and harvest.

dinka_abuk.name: watches over women, gardens and grain as the first woman and chief female divinity
dinka_abuk.notes: Abuk, first woman shaped with Garang from clay, stretched the single daily grain into paste; patroness of all women and cultivation.

dinka_garang.name: is the first man, shaped from clay and paired with Abuk
dinka_garang.notes: Free-divinity associated with men; the Creator made Abuk and Garang, the first pair, from the rich clay of the land.

dinka_garang.name: sends fevers yet also empowers the healers who cure them
dinka_garang.notes: Lienhardt records Garang as both a source of misfortune (fevers) and a healer-divinity.

dinka_nhialic.name: creates and upholds all life as supreme Divinity, sky and rain
dinka_nhialic.notes: Distant supreme creator of the sky who encompasses the free- and clan-divinities; bulls and oxen are sacrificed to him.

dinka_nhialic.name: withdraws to the sky and severs the rope between heaven and earth after the first offense
dinka_nhialic.notes: When Abuk's hoe struck him, Nhialic sent the bird atoc to cut the rope joining men to the sky, ending the age of plenty.

dogon_lebe.name: renews the fertility of the soil each season as the spirit of the earth
dogon_lebe.notes: Lébé Séru, first ancestor who died and returned as a great serpent, governs earth, vegetation and the periodic renewal of the fields.

dogon_binou_serou.name: manifests to his descendants as the clan's totem animal at the Binu shrine
dogon_binou_serou.notes: Immortal ancestor of the time before death; founder of the Ono lineage and eponym of the totemic Binu cult, he reveals himself as the clan totem.

desana_vai_mahse.name: guards the game within the hills and grants or withholds it to keep the balance of the hunt
desana_vai_mahse.notes: Master of Animals of the Vaupés; he keeps the creatures inside the hills and watches that hunters do not take more than their due.

desana_pamuri_mahse.name: leads the first humanity up the rivers in the living Snake-Canoe to settle the Vaupés
desana_pamuri_mahse.notes: Emissary sent by the Sun-Father, bearing his staff; the canoe in which he travels is itself a great anaconda swimming on the river-bottom.

desana_sun_father.name: creates and sustains the world with his yellow seminal light
desana_sun_father.notes: The invisible Sun-Father (Pagÿ Abé) generates and fertilizes creation through the yellow light/seminal power that is the central theme of Desana cosmology.

desana_sun_father.name: sends Pamurí-mahsë to people the earth and the Daughter of the Sun who bears the vine
desana_sun_father.notes: He dispatches his emissary in the Snake-Canoe and is father of the Yajé/Daughter of the Sun.

circassian_sosruquo.name: the bowl of fire stolen from the giant

circassian_mezitha.name: the golden-bristled boar he rides through the forest

dine_johonaai.name: the turquoise house in the eastern sky

dayak_jata.name: the golden water-gate (Balawang Bulau) of the underworld

crow_old_man_coyote.name: the handful of mud raised by Hell-Diver duck, from which he forms the earth

sources.reference: Lib @ Little Big Horn College, 'Creation Story'

dacian_zalmoxis.name: the three spears on which the chosen messenger is flung to carry word to the god

sources.reference: J. Colarusso, 'The Woman of the Myths: the Satanaya Cycle'
J. Colarusso, Nart Sagas from the Caucasus (Princeton, 2002)

dacian_burebista.gloss: Burebista (Greek transmission of the king's name)

crow_old_man_coyote.gloss: the one who made everything / First-Maker

circassian_shible.name: Shible-Wuj, the dance round the lightning-struck
circassian_shible.cadence: on occasion of a lightning strike
circassian_shible.notes: When lightning struck a place, beast or person, a circle (wuj) formed round the spot and a round-dance was performed with the 'Song of Lightning' (Щыблэ уэрэд), the names Shible and Yelle (Ilya) repeated in the chant. Those killed by lightning were buried with honor as blessed.

circassian_sozeresh.name: Sozeresh festival of the first days of spring
circassian_sozeresh.cadence: first three days of spring, from the Circassian New Year (22 March)
circassian_sozeresh.notes: Sozeresh was honored as a domestic idol of a seven-knotted branch of hamshkhut (pear/hawthorn) wood kept in the family barn; the household feasted and prayed before it over the first three days of the New Year for the prosperity of the stores.

circassian_thagaledj.name: Thaghelej-Wuj, harvest dance for the grain-god
circassian_thagaledj.notes: A ritual round-dance dedicated to the deity of agriculture and abundance, performed during the harvest festivals to secure a good crop.

circassian_mezitha.name: hunters' sacrifice to the lord of game
circassian_mezitha.notes: Hunters honored Mezithe with sacrifice (bulls or lambs), processions, dances and libations of the sacred brew sana, invoking him for luck and a share of the game.

circassian_tlepsh.name: smiths' vigil at the forge of Tlepsh
circassian_tlepsh.notes: Smiths revered Tlepsh as master of fire and metal; the community petitioned him at ritual vigils held at the forge or anvil to heal wounds and cure illness.

circassian_akhin.name: sacrifice of Akhin's self-walking cow
circassian_akhin.notes: Ahin, ranked among the most vital deities, was honored in the myth-feast of the sacred 'self-walking' cow that came of its own accord to the sacrifice for the prospering of the herds.

dacian_zalmoxis.name: the quadrennial messenger sent to Zalmoxis
dacian_zalmoxis.notes: Every fourth year the Getae chose a man by lot and flung him onto three upheld spears to carry their petitions to Zalmoxis; if he died pierced the god was thought favorable. Only the king and his messengers might approach the god's cave on Kogaionon.

dinka_nhialic.name: ox-sacrifice with the fishing-spear
dinka_nhialic.notes: A bull or ox is sacrificed to Nhialic; the invokers hold fishing-spears and call upon the clan-divinities, free-divinities, ancestral spirits and at times Nhialic himself.

dogon_lebe.name: cult of the Lébé earth-altar
dogon_lebe.notes: At the Lébé altar the Hogon (priest) makes offerings for the renewal of the soil; the serpent Lébé is said to lick the Hogon each night to transmit life-force to the fields.

dogon_binou_serou.name: the Binu totemic cult
dogon_binou_serou.notes: At the painted Binu shrines (gina), priests of the lineage make agricultural sacrifices and millet-porridge offerings to the immortal Binu ancestor, who appears as the clan totem.

dogon_dyongou_serou.name: the Sigui rite and the masks
dogon_dyongou_serou.notes: The death of Dyongou Sérou, the first being to die, founded the great mask cult; the Sigui, held roughly every sixty years over several years, commemorates the first ancestor and renews the Great Mask (imina na).

dayak_tempon_telon.name: the Tiwah secondary mortuary feast
dayak_tempon_telon.cadence: secondary funeral, held in due course after death
dayak_tempon_telon.notes: In the great Tiwah ceremony the soul (liau) is released and conveyed by Tempon Telon's soul-ship to the highest heaven, Lewu Tatau; the corpse is laid in a boat-shaped coffin reflecting that journey.

attributes.name: ginger-red moustache, great antlers and golden-red topknot
attributes.notes: Circassian sources picture Mezithe with a ginger-red moustache, two great antlers and a golden-red topknot.

attributes.name: two sparrows perched on his shoulders
attributes.notes: Two sparrows sit on the hunt-god's shoulders as he rides.

attributes.name: stone-born hero standing on a high rock holding aloft the bowl of stolen fire
attributes.notes: The visual shorthand of the whole Nart cycle in modern Caucasian art (e.g. the Sosruko monument at Nalchik): the small hero on a crag, fire-bowl raised over his head.

sacredPlants.name: the lightning-struck tree/grove (made holy by his bolt)

attributes.name: domestic idol of a seven-knotted branch of pear/hawthorn (hamshkhut) wood
attributes.notes: Kept in the family barn and brought out at the spring festival; the post embodies the god of the household stores.

attributes.name: identified as White Shell Woman and Turquoise Woman
attributes.notes: Also called Abalone and Jet Woman; her four aspects answer to the four sacred jewels and the four seasons of youth, maturity, age and renewal.

attributes.name: the turquoise sun-disk borne as a shield across the sky
attributes.notes: Jóhonaaʼéí carries the sun on its daily course and dwells in a turquoise house in the east.

attributes.name: dweller atop Spider Rock in Canyon de Chelly
attributes.notes: Said to sit on the sandstone spire watching the land; the rock is told to be whitened by sun-bleached bones.

sacredAnimals.name: the spider (her form and the source of the weaving-gift)
the small snake (her sacred animal and form)
the hornbill (Tingang), his upperworld form and the male cosmic symbol

sacredPlants.name: the Tree of Life (batang garing) grown from his cast-away golden head-band

sacredAnimals.name: the water-snake / dragon (Tambon), her underworld form and the female cosmic symbol
the Hell-Diver duck (his diving brother who fetches the earth-mud)

sources.reference: Lib @ Little Big Horn College, 'Creation Story'

sacredAnimals.name: the muskrat (wîcahk's diver who fetches the mud to remake the earth)

attributes.name: a small red dwarf-figure who can change shape
attributes.notes: Reichel-Dolmatoff's Desana picture Vaí-mahsë as a small red being able to appear in many forms.

attributes.name: bears the Sun-Father's staff as the emissary of creation
attributes.notes: He carries the Sun-Father's staff while searching the Vaupés for the place to settle humanity.

sacredAnimals.name: the anaconda that is the living Snake-Canoe
